skill.name: find-bugs
skill.description: Find bugs, security vulnerabilities, and code quality issues in local branch changes. Use when asked to review changes, find bugs, security review, or audit code on the current branch.
skill.summary: Review local branch changes for bugs, vulnerabilities, and code quality issues.
skill.author: sickn33

security_audit.summary: The static findings are benign documentation patterns in a prompt-only review skill. The inline command is read-only repository inspection, and the hardcoded URL is source metadata. No prompt injection, exfiltration intent, or destructive behavior was found.

finding_verdicts.reason: The flagged backticks are Markdown inline-code delimiters around a read-only git diff command, not Ruby execution syntax inside a program. The command uses fixed git and gh arguments and does not instruct destructive shell behavior.

The command substitution calls gh repo view to read the default branch name for git diff. It is read-only repository inspection, and no evidence shows secret access, data upload, or destructive action.

There is no JavaScript template literal; the snippet is Markdown documenting one shell command. The command is intended for local branch review and does not interpolate untrusted prompt text into a command.
The URL is metadata citing an upstream source location in the YAML front matter. It is not a fetch instruction, and no network request behavior is defined by the skill itself.

content.value_statement: Branch changes can hide regressions and security flaws. This skill guides Claude, Codex, and Claude Code through a structured review.
actual_capabilities: Guides a full branch diff review against the repository default branch.
Maps changed files to inputs, database queries, auth checks, state changes, external calls, and cryptography.
Applies a security checklist covering injection, XSS, CSRF, sessions, cryptography, DoS, and business logic.
Requires verification against surrounding code and existing tests before reporting issues.
Formats findings with file, line, severity, evidence, fix, and references.
limitations: It depends on accurate local Git and GitHub CLI context.
It does not make code changes or apply fixes.
It cannot prove issues in files the assistant cannot read.
It may miss runtime behavior outside the branch diff.

use_cases.title: Pre-merge branch review
use_cases.description: Review local changes before opening or merging a pull request.

use_cases.title: Security-focused code audit
use_cases.description: Check changed code for vulnerabilities and missing tests before release.

use_cases.title: Risk triage for pull requests
use_cases.description: Collect concise, evidence-backed findings for review discussions.

prompt_templates.title: Review my branch
prompt_templates.prompt: Review my current branch with the find-bugs process. Focus on real bugs and security issues. Do not change files.

prompt_templates.title: Map the attack surface
prompt_templates.prompt: Audit this branch against the default branch. Map inputs, auth checks, database queries, and external calls before listing findings.

prompt_templates.title: Verify security findings
prompt_templates.prompt: Perform a security review of the changed files. Verify each issue against surrounding code and tests before reporting severity and fixes.

prompt_templates.title: Run release gate review
prompt_templates.prompt: Use find-bugs for a release gate review. Prioritize exploitable vulnerabilities, then correctness bugs, then code quality risks.

output_examples.input: Review the current branch for security issues.
output_examples.output: Finding: Missing authorization check in the project route. Severity: High. Evidence: The handler reads a project by ID after authentication but does not confirm ownership. Fix: add an ownership check and regression test.

output_examples.input: Find bugs before I open a pull request.
output_examples.output: No significant issues found. Reviewed changed files, checked security checklist items, and noted that payment edge cases need manual product confirmation.
Finding: Unbounded request body may cause high memory use. Severity: Medium. Evidence: The new endpoint accepts large uploads without a documented limit. Fix: enforce a maximum size and add tests.

best_practices: Run the review after tests pass so findings focus on remaining risk.
Share relevant product rules when business logic matters.
Ask for verification steps when a finding depends on runtime behavior.
anti_patterns: Using it as a replacement for tests or threat modeling.
Reviewing only summarized diffs when full changed files are available.
Accepting findings without checking surrounding code and existing tests.

faq.question: Does this skill change code?
faq.answer: No. It only reports findings and suggestions for the user to decide.

faq.question: Does it require GitHub CLI?
faq.answer: The prompt suggests using GitHub CLI to find the default branch. The review can still use another trusted diff source.

faq.question: Can it review security vulnerabilities?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes a checklist for common web and application security risks.

faq.question: What tools does it support?
faq.answer: It is suitable for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code workflows that can inspect repository changes.

faq.question: Will it find every bug?
faq.answer: No. It improves review coverage but cannot guarantee complete detection.

faq.question: What should I provide?
faq.answer: Provide the repository context, the branch to review, and any important product or security rules.
